title: Instructions
summary: Brief for Capstone Project 2: build a personal portfolio site using only HTML and CSS. There is no solution walkthrough because capstones are meant to be the learner's own work.

concepts.heading: Capstone project ground rules
points: Capstones have no solution code, no video walkthrough and no design spec, so the finished site can be presented as original work in a portfolio.
Getting stuck is the point: gaps in memory show which earlier lessons or docs to revisit.
Deliverables are one HTML file, one CSS file and any images used. No JavaScript is allowed in this project.
A live example site exists at appbrewery.github.io/capstone-2-example for visual inspiration.

concepts.heading: Required features
points: Hero section giving a short introduction to you and your background.
Resume page or section listing education, work experience, skills and other details (may link to Capstone 1).
Contact section with ways to get in touch.

concepts.heading: Technical requirements
points: Valid HTML using semantic elements (header, nav, main, section, footer).
Valid CSS with sensible naming and organisation.
Responsive layout that works across screen sizes and devices.
Every image needs meaningful alt text.

concepts.heading: Suggested five-hour timeline
points: Hour 1: collect content and design ideas, sketch wireframes and mockups.
Hours 2-3: write the HTML structure and CSS, testing in different browsers and devices.
Hour 4: finalise design and copy, revise, optimise performance.
Hour 5: launch, share in the Q&A for feedback, make final tweaks.

task.name: Capstone 2: Personal portfolio site
task.starting_point: Empty project; you create index.html, styles.css and an images folder.
task.goal: A responsive, semantic, accessible, HTML+CSS-only personal website with hero, resume, projects, about and contact sections.
steps: Plan content and sketch a wireframe of each section.
Write semantic HTML for the hero, resume, projects, about and contact sections.
Style with an external stylesheet; make it responsive with media queries or flexible layouts.
Add alt text to every image.
Validate HTML and CSS, test on several screen sizes, then share for feedback.
task.expected_result: A polished portfolio page with all five sections and no JavaScript.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 13 - Capstone Project 2 - Personal Site/ (one student's own site: index.html, styles.css, imgs/)

pitfalls: (Extra) The reference repo copy includes a script.js with theme toggle and mobile menu code, which breaks the brief's no-JavaScript rule; also it contains the student's personal name and email, which should be ignored.
Forgetting alt text or a viewport meta tag, which hurt accessibility and responsiveness.

gaps_and_ideas: Add a capstone-style lesson: blurb 'Build a one-page portfolio with only HTML and CSS'.
Tasks: (1) semantic skeleton with header/nav/main/sections/footer, (2) hero with image and heading, (3) projects grid with flexbox or grid, (4) responsive media query, (5) alt text audit.
Starter code idea: a skeleton with empty section tags and a TODO comment in each.
Interactive demo idea: a checklist that inspects the learner's editor HTML for required sections and alt attributes.
